forces.title: High client wallet volatility in CIB challenges incumbent banks
forces.description: Corporate and institutional clients, including financial sponsors, are increasingly reallocating 12-25% of their annual banking wallet. This shift is driven by performance, event-driven changes (M&A, capital restructuring), and strategic rebalancing. Investment banks must recognize that relationships are no longer guaranteed and proactively target contestable flow and event products like M&A and capital markets mandates to retain or grow share, rather than relying on sticky operational core business.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Growing competition for UK midmarket investment banking and advisory mandates
forces.description: UK and global banks are actively expanding their investment banking teams to target the midmarket segment, intensifying competition. This trend directly challenges established incumbents' corporate relationships and their ability to secure advisory mandates, especially those stemming from commercial banking client formation or business owner exits. Banks must strengthen their integrated offerings across commercial, investment, and private banking to defend and capture these valuable relationships.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Nonbank market makers gaining significant share in commoditized flow products
forces.description: Nonbank market makers (NBMMs) are capturing 9-14% of wallet share in electronic and commoditized flow products like cash equities and ETFs. Their advantage lies in technological sophistication, superior liquidity provision, and proven risk management, coupled with speed and low-cost execution. This poses a direct threat to traditional stockbrokers and investment bank desks dealing in high-volume, low-margin flow products, pushing them to differentiate beyond price or risk losing market share.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Execution certainty and relationship strength paramount in CIB provider selection
forces.description: Beyond pricing, corporate clients, institutional investors, and financial sponsors increasingly prioritize execution certainty and strong historical relationships when selecting financing and lending providers. For M&A and capital markets mandates, operational reliability, deal closure assurance, and sector expertise are highly valued. This emphasizes the need for investment banks to build trust and deliver exceptional service, offering a stronger competitive advantage than product features or price alone, particularly for securing anchor bank status.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Diversification of UK financial services trade towards fast-growing Asian markets
forces.description: The UK's financial services trade is gradually diversifying beyond its traditional anchors (EU and US) towards high-growth markets in Asia (China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan, South Korea, Australia) and the GCC. China, Hong Kong, and Singapore show particularly fast average annual growth rates. This expansion presents opportunities for UK investment banks and brokers to intermediate capital and provide specialist expertise in these emerging corridors, enhancing the sector's long-term resilience and growth prospects.
forces.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

forces.title: AI-enabled automation reshaping corporate and investment banking workflows
forces.description: Agentic AI is poised to significantly enhance productivity in corporate and investment banking by automating exception-heavy workflows such as onboarding, KYC checks, trade controls, collateral, and settlement. Specialized AI agents can coordinate these processes end-to-end, maintaining human oversight, and compressing timelines from weeks to days. This allows banks to move at "AI speed" in product development and technology modernization, offering a critical competitive edge and improving cost-to-income ratios.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Heightened importance of purchase price in private equity deals for M&A advisory
forces.description: Private equity investors are increasingly prioritizing purchase price discipline, especially for post-2018 buyout vintages where high entry multiples have compressed returns. With global buyout multiples at record highs, the margin for error has significantly shrunk. This trend implies a more discerning M&A environment, where investment banks advising PE clients will need to focus on delivering clear value and optimal deal structuring, potentially affecting deal volumes and fee structures if valuations become prohibitive.
forces.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

forces.title: Favorable regulatory environment driving bank M&A activity
forces.description: In the US, a pro-consolidation regulatory agenda, including faster deal approvals and eased antitrust scrutiny for smaller banks, is creating ideal conditions for M&A. This regulatory shift, combined with trends like AI-related cost reduction, is expected to fuel a significant wave of consolidation in commercial banking for two to three years. While US-specific, such regulatory support for M&A, if replicated or influencing global sentiment, could bolster investment banking deal origination and advisory services.
forces.source_title: Hidden Gems: How to Find the US Bank M&A Targets Everyone Else Is Missing

forces.title: Corporates increasingly opt for nonbank financing over traditional banking
forces.description: Approximately 40% of corporates are open to using nonbank financing, with 17% looking to fintechs and 22% to private credit/direct institutional lending over the next three years. Financial sponsors are also extensively utilizing direct lenders and private credit firms. These nonbank providers offer structured flexibility, speed, and digital experiences, challenging traditional banks for financing mandates. Investment banks must enhance their offerings in these areas or risk losing contestable wallet share to agile nonbank competitors.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: AI-enabled relationship managers crucial for competitive advantage
forces.description: Clients prioritize relationship managers (RMs) who are fast, responsive, and deeply understand their needs. AI tools can empower RMs by automating routine tasks, centralizing client knowledge, and delivering consistent service. This allows RMs to focus on higher-value advisory, sector expertise, and orchestrating comprehensive solutions. Banks investing in AI-enabled front offices and client-centric capabilities can redefine the value of an anchor bank relationship, securing and deepening client mandates in investment banking.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

forces.title: Fintechs increasingly acquire banks or secure charters, blurring competitive lines
forces.description: A growing number of fintech, crypto, and payments firms are seeking or obtaining US bank charters, while some are directly acquiring banks. This trend indicates fintechs are moving beyond pure tech and into regulated banking, gaining access to deposit funding and balance sheets. This convergence creates new competitive dynamics for traditional investment banks, as fintechs become more formidable rivals or potential M&A targets, requiring strategic responses from incumbents.
forces.source_title: Hidden Gems: How to Find the US Bank M&A Targets Everyone Else Is Missing

viewpoints.title: UK financial services exports diversifying, with capital markets opportunities in Asia
viewpoints.description: The UK's financial services exports are heavily concentrated in the EU and US, accounting for two-thirds of total growth over the past two decades. However, there's a visible diversification towards fast-growing markets like China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and the GCC, which are increasingly crucial for future trade prospects. The UK industry needs to assess how its capabilities, including in capital markets, can service these emerging corridors more effectively to capture new growth opportunities and enhance economic resilience.
viewpoints.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

viewpoints.title: Corporate and Investment Banking wallet share highly fluid, requires continuous re-earning
viewpoints.description: Banking relationships are no longer evergreen, with 12-25% of the annual banking wallet being reallocated by clients each year across corporate, institutional investor, and financial sponsor segments. While operational cash management remains sticky, flow products like FX, hedging, and M&A/capital markets mandates are highly contestable. Banks must continuously re-earn business by prioritizing service, delivery, and targeting event-driven products to maintain anchor status and avoid being relegated to utility roles.
viewpoints.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

viewpoints.title: Intensified competition in UK midmarket investment banking and advisory mandates
viewpoints.description: The UK banking sector is experiencing intensified competition at the intersection of commercial, investment, and private banking. Several UK and global banks are launching investment-banking teams to target the midmarket segment, challenging incumbents. For entrepreneurs, commercial relationships are vital as they can lead to significant personal wealth and advisory mandates post-exit. Banks must actively defend these corporate relationships and advisory opportunities to prevent losing value to challengers and other platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Private equity deal pricing now critical for returns amidst high entry multiples
viewpoints.description: The axiom "you make your money on the buy" has reasserted itself in private equity. For 2018–2023 buyout vintages, disciplined buyers in the lowest-price quartile significantly outperformed those who paid high multiples. While global buyout entry multiples rose to a record 11.8x EBITDA in 2025, and 18.1x for larger transactions, such premiums shrink the margin for error. This trend emphasizes the importance of purchase price discipline for M&A success, impacting investment banking deal advisory.
viewpoints.source_title: Private equity confirms a timeless principle: Purchase price matters

viewpoints.title: US commercial banking M&A expected to surge, driven by capabilities and regulatory support
viewpoints.description: The US commercial banking sector is poised for a significant consolidation wave, with expectations that at least one more bank will exceed $1 trillion in assets by 2030 through M&A. This trend is bolstered by favorable regulatory conditions, including faster deal approvals and eased antitrust scrutiny under $250 billion in assets. Banks are increasingly seeking capability-led acquisitions, particularly in fintech, to enhance digital technology and AI readiness, suggesting a strong M&A environment for investment banks.
viewpoints.source_title: Hidden Gems: How to Find the US Bank M&A Targets Everyone Else Is Missing

new_opportunities.description: Banks are seeking to buy fintech challengers to extend their capabilities in digital technology and AI, opening up new M&A advisory opportunities for investment banks.

market_sizing.methodology: Value of announced deals in US commercial banking. Announced deals in US commercial banking grew 19% in 2025 and 7% year-over-year in H1 2026.

demand_drivers.description: The EU and US remain primary drivers of growth for UK financial services trade due to long-standing core relationships.

Fast-growing markets in Asia (China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Japan, Asia-Pacific Other) and the GCC are contributing meaningfully to trade growth, driving demand for UK financial services expertise, including capital markets services.

new_opportunities.description: The gradual shift in global financial services trade towards smaller, faster-growing corridors in Asia and the Middle East presents opportunities for UK capital markets expertise, requiring granular assessment of UK capabilities and local partnerships.

market_sizing.methodology: Total growth in UK financial services trade (exports + imports) over 20 years. The EU and US accounted for around two-thirds of the total 167.5% growth.
market_sizing.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

This competitive deal environment can impact the economics of M&A for buyers, and by extension, the fees for investment banks, especially if deals become harder to close profitably or demand more structured advisory.
